steps.tx: **Monogenic autoinflammatory syndromes** are inherited disorders of innate immunity characterized by recurrent unprovoked episodes of sterile systemic inflammation. In contrast to autoimmune disorders, autoinflammatory diseases exhibit **hyperactivation of innate immune pathways** with zero high-titer autoantibodies or antigen-specific autoreactive T cells.
steps.say: Monogenic autoinflammatory syndromes are inherited disorders of innate immunity. They feature recurrent sterile inflammation without high-titer autoantibodies or antigen-specific T cells.

vis.alt: Innate immune hyperactivation in monogenic autoinflammatory syndromes
vis.caption: Autoinflammatory syndromes arise from innate immune dysregulation without autoantibodies. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Familial Mediterranean fever** or FMF is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by **MEFV mutations** encoding pyrin. Attacks characteristically last **12 to 72 hours**, featuring high spiking fever, sterile peritonitis, pleuritis, and an **erysipelas-like erythema** over the lower leg. Lifelong daily oral **colchicine** prevents recurrent attacks and lethal renal AA amyloidosis.
steps.say: Familial Mediterranean fever is caused by recessive MEFV mutations. Attacks last 12 to 72 hours with fever, serositis, and erysipelas-like rash, treated with lifelong colchicine.

vis.alt: MEFV pyrin mutations, peritonitis, and colchicine therapy in FMF
vis.caption: Familial Mediterranean fever presents with episodic serositis and requires lifelong colchicine. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes** or CAPS are autosomal dominant conditions caused by gain-of-function **NLRP3 mutations**. CAPS comprises a severity continuum: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, **Muckle-Wells syndrome** featuring urticaria, progressive sensorineural deafness, and amyloidosis, and severe neonatal-onset **NOMID/CINCA**. All forms respond dramatically to **IL-1 blockade** with anakinra or canakinumab.
steps.say: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes arise from gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations. Muckle-Wells features cold urticaria and progressive deafness, responding promptly to IL-1 blockade.

rows: Sensorineural hearing loss, chronic urticaria, AA amyloidosis
Chronic aseptic meningitis, patellar epiphyseal overgrowth, papilledema

steps.tx: **TNF Receptor-Associated Periodic Syndrome** or TRAPS is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by **TNFRSF1A mutations** encoding the 55-kDa TNF receptor. TRAPS is distinguished by prolonged inflammatory episodes lasting **1 to 3 weeks**, marked by migratory myalgias with monocytic fasciitis, painful periorbital edema, and high risk of **AA amyloidosis**, responding to IL-1 inhibitors.
steps.say: TRAPS is caused by dominant TNFRSF1A mutations with prolonged attacks lasting 1 to 3 weeks. Typical findings include migratory myalgias, periorbital edema, and amyloidosis risk.

nodes.label: Misfolded mutant 55-kDa TNF receptor retained in endoplasmic reticulum
Prolonged attacks (1 to 3 weeks) with myalgia and periorbital edema
Dramatic therapeutic response to IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra

steps.tx: **Mevalonate kinase deficiency** or Hyper-IgD syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by **MVK mutations** in cholesterol biosynthesis. Attacks occur every **4 to 6 weeks**, lasting 3 to 7 days, frequently provoked by childhood vaccinations. Features include painful cervical lymphadenopathy, aphthous ulcers, abdominal pain, and elevated serum **IgD and IgA**.
steps.say: Mevalonate kinase deficiency presents with fever episodes triggered by vaccinations. Attacks feature cervical lymphadenopathy, oral aphthae, and elevated IgD and IgA.

rows: Episodes last 3 to 7 days every 4 to 6 weeks
Elevated serum IgD and IgA, urinary mevalonic acid
Mevalonic acid elevated during active febrile episodes

steps.tx: **Blau syndrome** is an autosomal dominant pediatric granulomatous autoinflammatory disorder caused by gain-of-function **NOD2** or CARD15 mutations. It is clinically defined by the classic triad of **granulomatous polyarthritis**, **panuveitis**, and **camptodactyly** with a brownish-tan papular cutaneous rash.
steps.say: Blau syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by NOD2 mutations. The classic triad comprises granulomatous polyarthritis, panuveitis, and camptodactyly.

steps.tx: **PAPA syndrome** or Pyogenic Arthritis, Pyoderma gangrenosum, and Acne is an autosomal dominant condition caused by **PSTPIP1 mutations**. Defective hyperphosphorylation drives hyperactive uninhibited binding to pyrin, provoking massive sterile neutrophilic joint destruction, recurrent pyogenic monoarthritis, and destructive ulcerating **pyoderma gangrenosum**.
steps.say: PAPA syndrome is caused by PSTPIP1 mutations altering pyrin binding. Patients suffer sterile pyogenic arthritis, severe cystic acne, and pyoderma gangrenosum.

nodes.label: Excessive interleukin-1-beta processing and neutrophil influx
Sterile pyogenic arthritis and severe pyoderma gangrenosum

steps.tx: **Type I interferonopathies** including Aicardi-Goutières syndrome and **SAVI** or STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy are monogenic disorders marked by constitutive upregulation of type I interferons. Manifestations include severe microangiopathic telangiectasias, **chilblains**, intracranial calcifications, and interstitial pulmonary fibrosis, responding to **JAK inhibitors**.
steps.say: Type one interferonopathies like SAVI exhibit constitutive interferon signaling. Features include microangiopathy, chilblains, and lung fibrosis, responsive to JAK inhibitors.

rows: Severe digital necrosis, chilblains, pulmonary fibrosis
